A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RMNP research work. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPT-2 and LLaMA pretraining results, optimizer timing measurements, learning-rate sweeps and diagonal-dominance analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds larger-model experiments, additional optimizer comparisons, ablations, Mamba pretraining and ResNet-18/CIFAR-10 results.

M1.justification: The proposed optimizer still updates momentum and applies row-wise L2 normalization. The revised Gram-matrix expressions reconcile the equations with the row normalization already specified in v1's Equation 4 and Appendix A. The expanded experiments and revised training prescriptions do not introduce a new core optimization mechanism.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates language-model pretraining on OpenWebText, FineWeb-Edu-100B and C4. v3 retains these tasks and adds CIFAR-10 image classification in Appendix E.6, substantially extending coverage to a different modality and task. Larger language models and Mamba change model configurations within language modeling.

E2.justification: v3 adds evaluated Shampoo and SOAP learning-rate sweeps to the LLaMA-60M and LLaMA-130M comparisons in Tables 11–12. The corresponding v1 Tables 12–13 contain only Muon and RMNP. Shampoo and SOAP were cited in v1, but these direct experimental comparisons are new.

E3.justification: v3 adds GPT-2 1.5B and LLaMA-1B pretraining, Mamba and ResNet configurations, doubled training budgets, parameter-group ablations and clipping diagnostics. Appendix D also reports shared AdamW/matrix learning rates for LLaMA RMNP, replacing v1's independently fixed AdamW-rate prescription, and reverses the stated shape multiplier from max(1,sqrt(n/m)) to max(1,sqrt(m/n)). These reported setting revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's learning-rate sweeps and Transformer diagonal-dominance analyses, v3 tests whether advantages persist with twice the training budget and whether assigning embeddings and the LM head to the matrix optimizer matters (Appendices D.3–D.4). It also adds larger-model, Mamba and ResNet dominance diagnostics and gradient-clipping analyses (Appendices B and E).

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed-based variability, confidence intervals or significance tests for the experimental comparisons. Raw and smoothed diagnostic trajectories and averages across parameters are not newly introduced uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Retained perplexity and timing tables preserve their values, while v3 adds substantial results. Examples include RMNP/Muon perplexities of 12.58/12.97 for GPT-2 1.5B and 13.75/14.13 for LLaMA-1B (Tables 18–19). New sweeps report best Mamba perplexities of 32.32/32.95 and CIFAR-10 accuracies of 94.33%/94.65% (Tables 20–21). Additional baseline and ablation results expand the evidence under new settings.

T1.justification: v3 corrects the order of diagonal extraction and matrix powers in Algorithm 2 and Equations 3–4, making the preconditioner expression agree with row normalization. It also marks finite Newton–Schulz orthogonalization as approximate and clarifies the matrix-dimension/transposition convention. The convergence theorems and Appendix A proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract newly claims empirical asymptotic equivalence between orthogonalization and row-wise normalization for Transformers. This substantially strengthens v1's claims of comparable optimization performance and observed diagonal dominance. The principal computational-complexity and convergence claims remain, while the conclusion extends the empirical claims to larger models.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations concerning generalization beyond Transformers, persistence under longer training, negligible embedding/head effects and reduced gradient-norm volatility. It also acknowledges that LLaMA-1B lacks a full learning-rate sweep. Some interpretations exceed the displayed evidence: Appendix D.4's claim that differences stay within 0.13 PPL conflicts with Tables 11 and 15, where best Muon-60M perplexity changes from 29.58 to 29.38.

D1.justification: Appendices D–E expand the documented training recipes with explicit embedding/head assignments, LLaMA learning-rate conventions, larger-model configurations, LLaMA-1B hardware and fixed hyperparameters, and Mamba/ResNet learning-rate grids. The embedded code pointer also changes from an anonymous 4open repository to a named GitHub repository; external availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds substantive discussion of Adam-mini, SRON, SCALE, SWAN, MNGD, Mano and MOGA. It acknowledges earlier row-normalization approaches and expands the distinction between curvature-based explanations and worst-case steepest-descent analyses. Pethick et al. was already discussed in v1; its relocation accompanies a broader revision of research positioning.

P1.justification: Most existing prose, the six-section main structure and the proof appendix remain intact. v3 expands Section 2, replaces the former discussion at the end of Section 3.2, adds an appendix contents list and organizes new material into Appendices D.3–D.4 and E. These are localized editorial and organizational changes rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: v3 adds a conceptual Figure 3, revises Figure 2's formulas, combines global dominance plots using relative training progress, and merges and expands the main performance charts. Numerous training, ablation and clipping displays are added, alongside expanded comparison tables. Several earlier plots and scores are relocated or redisplayed rather than newly generated evidence.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the added competitors, longer-training checks, vision experiments and corrected preconditioner equations improve the evidential basis and technical clarity. These gains are tempered by the stronger asymptotic-equivalence claim, which the finite-scale dominance diagnostics do not establish, and inaccurate new interpretations such as Appendix D.4's 0.13-PPL bound. The resulting net quality improvement is limited despite the substantial expansion.
